explanation.title: Swiss Franc Stablecoin
explanation.description: Frankencoin (ZCHF) is a digital currency that maintains a stable 1:1 value with the Swiss franc. It combines the stability of Switzerland's trusted currency with the transparency and openness of the blockchain.

explanation.title: Fully Decentralized
explanation.description: Unlike centralized stablecoins, the value of the Frankencoin does not depend on an issuer that guarantees its value. Instead, the Frankencoin is backed by on-chain collateral that can be liquidated if necessary to maintain its value.

explanation.title: Live and Established
explanation.description: Frankencoin has been deployed on 8 different blockchains. It is the largest and most popular Swiss franc stablecoin, enabling on-chain transactions in Swiss francs since 2023 with no significant deviations from its peg.

how_it_works.title: The Frankencoin System at a Glance
how_it_works.subtitle: Frankencoin is a fully transparent, rule-based, decentralized, modular, and neutral financial infrastructure.

description.content: Frankencoins can be created by anyone that deposits a suitable collateral.
The collateral remains locked until its owner returns the created Frankencoins (plus fees) again.
Newly minted Frankencoins are typically sold in the market.
Users can buy Frankencoins on various trading venues.
They might want to use Frankencoins to make Swiss franc payments in DeFi or elsewhere.
Recipients may want to sell the collected Frankencoins again.
When swapping Swiss francs into Frankencoins on the market,
and then storing them in the savings module,
users can earn an attractive interest.
Users can invest ZCHF through FCS to support the system's equity reserve.
The FCS contract invests in the underlying Equity token, FPS, and issues one FCS per FPS.
Redemption into ZCHF depends on the contract's eligibility rules, pricing curve, fees and redemption discount.

explanation.title: Collateralized debt position
explanation.description: Frankencoin operates as a decentralized collateralized debt position system. Users deposit crypto assets as collateral to mint digital Swiss francs (ZCHF). The collateral remains under the user's control while securing the outstanding franc issuance, similar to a secured lending facility with transparent, automated terms.

explanation.title: Why 1 ZCHF equals 1 CHF
explanation.description: Frankencoins are over-collateralized, such that each Frankencoin is always backed by at least one Swiss franc worth of assets. The assets backing the Frankencoins are publicly visible on-chain.

explanation.title: Market-driven price stability
explanation.description: The system is designed to keep the long-term value of the Frankencoin in line with the Swiss franc. This means that every short-term deviation is an arbitrage opportunity for the market to exploit, thereby keeping the exchange rate close to parity.

regulatory.title: Legal Classification & MiCA Compliance
regulatory.description: Frankencoin operates in full compliance with Swiss and European Union regulations. Independent legal assessments by LEXR confirm that ZCHF can be used without restrictions as a payment token and that MiCA’s issuer obligations under Titles II, III and IV do not apply due to ZCHF’s decentralised design and lack of an identifiable issuer. In addition, a MiCA-format ZCHF white paper has been published and appears in ESMA’s Interim MiCA Register for crypto-assets other than ARTs and EMTs.

cover.title: Optional Depeg Cover
cover.description: ZCHF holders can now protect themselves against a sustained loss of the peg. Depeg Cover — underwritten by Nexus Mutual and available through OpenCover — pays out if Frankencoin trades 10% or more below 1 CHF for seven consecutive days. This is an optional, third-party product, not offered by the Frankencoin Association.

audits.description: The Frankencoin and each added component has been audited by leading blockchain security firms. The audits cover smart contract security, economic design, and overall system integrity to ensure a robust and secure platform for users.

foundation.title: Theoretical Foundation
foundation.description: The Frankencoin was conceived a part of [a PhD thesis](https://www.zora.uzh.ch/entities/publication/b1bff836-6852-457d-93e6-496807db37fa) completed at the Department of Finance at the University of Zurich. Among other things, it covers the game theory behind the system's novel liquidation mechanism, quantifies the risk of Bitcoin as a collateral, and it formally analyses the veto-based governance system. The Frankencoin system can be seen as a Continuous Capital Corporation, a concept introduced in chapter three denoting a company that issues and redeems shares autonomously according to fixed rules that are optimal under a wide range of theoretical assumptions.

how_simple.title: Three moving parts
how_simple.subtitle: Everything else on this site is detail. This is the system.

cards.title: 1 · Mint
cards.description: Anyone deposits collateral (BTC, ETH, tokenized shares, gold) and mints ZCHF against it. They pay interest upfront into the reserve.

cards.title: 2 · Keep the peg
cards.description: Every ZCHF is backed by more than one franc of collateral. Anyone can challenge a weak position; auctions settle it.

cards.title: 3 · Share the income
cards.description: Savers are paid the protocol rate from the reserve. What remains raises the value of FCS, the share token.
